newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Second S.Korean mobile phone operator cuts fees.
newsitem.headline: Second S.Korean mobile phone operator cuts fees.

text.p: Shinsegi Telecomm Inc, one of South Korea's two mobile telephone operators, said on Thursday it would sharply cut fees for new subscribers effective Saturday.
"We decided to cut costs for the subscribers on the grounds that the current service charges are too high," said a spokesman for Shinsegi.
It plans to cut the expense of deposits, sign-up fees and a handset to 360,000 won from around 700,000 won at present, he said.
Pohang Iron and Steel Co and Kolon Industries Inc are major shareholders of Shinsegi with a 15 percent and a 14 percent stake, respectively.
The Shinsegi spokesman said the company would also cut mobile phone charges by 20 percent in early September.
Korea Mobile Telecom Co had a monopoly in Korea's mobile phone service until Shinsegi launched its operations in April. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727-5646
